newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up led by banks, machine-tools.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up led by banks, machine-tools.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged up Friday led by banks and a machine-tool company rumored to be the target of German investors.

Bogota's IBB index gained 0.05 percent to close at 842.87 on a 1.07 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up 0.47 percent to finish at 13,450.27 on 3.741 billion pesos.

Bancoquia continued to rise in Bogota as investors jockeyed for position before the deal -- announced 10 days -- which will see Spain's Grupo Santander acquiring 55 percent of the bank. It ended up 1.98 percent at 2,570.

"Large packets of Bancoquia shares are hard to find right now because of the Grupo Santander deal. One or two shareholders decided to sell, but the heavy demand and limited supply forced up the price," one Bogota broker said.
Banco de Colombia gained 0.24 percent to end the session at 415.

The highlight of both the Bogota and Medellin exchanges was the little favored machine tool and industrial equipment manufacturer Distral SA, in which the U.S. Lancaster Steel Co. has a 33.07 percent stake.

Markets were awash with rumors that the company, one of the biggest of its kind in Colombia, was preparing a rights issue. Dealers said it was rumored that the new shares would be ceded to German investors. Distral SA rose 36 percent to 34 in Bogota and 20 percent in Medellin to close at 40.
"This was undoubtedly a cross-deal between existing shareholders who appear to be rearranging the portfolio in advance of heavy German investment," a Medellin broker said.
Brewing giant Bavaria gained 1.23 percent in Medellin to close at 4,099.99, while cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco was up 2.65 percent to 3,100.
